misconceptions.description: Putting open-ended to-dos on the calendar as all-day events instead of in a task list with due dates
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds 'write essay' as an all-day event that just rolls over each day, never marked done
misconceptions.feedback: Use the calendar for fixed-time commitments and a task list for work to do. A task carries a due date and a done state; an event blocks a time.

misconceptions.description: Capturing tasks with no due date so nothing surfaces before it is late
misconceptions.trigger: learner has a long undated task list and discovers an assignment the night it is due
misconceptions.feedback: Give every task a due date, then sort or filter by it. A list with no dates cannot warn you what is next.

misconceptions.description: Scheduling only the deadline and not the work time needed to meet it
misconceptions.trigger: learner blocks the 11:59 PM due time but never blocks the hours to do the work
misconceptions.feedback: Schedule a work block before the deadline, not just the deadline. The due time is when it is finished, not when you start.

misconceptions.description: Setting a reminder for the moment an event starts, leaving no lead time to prepare or travel
misconceptions.trigger: learner gets a 'class now' alert with zero minutes to walk over or open materials
misconceptions.feedback: Set reminder lead time that matches what you must do first, for example 20 minutes before to travel or prep.
